I feel so dumb for not realizing my cat just wanted to be included on my desk My six year old cat has been pretty vocal most of her life this far, but recently she’s been very persistent to keep my attention. For a few weeks I figured this was due to her recent issues with a prior UTI and her discomfort with a urinary crystal (scheduled to be removed next week), so I got her a low dose prescription for gabapentin. This calmed her down a tad, but it didn’t stop her from sitting next to my chair and nipping me for attention.

Today she was meowing anytime I looked away from her after I let her into the office, so I decided to look up specifically why cats might get more demanding when you sit to work at your desk. Well, turns out this is pretty common as most of you probably know. And the most common solution I found was to make a space on the desk for the cat to feel “included.” So I shuffled some things around to fit her bed next to my work equipment on the desk.

And wouldn’t you know it, this calmed her down immediately. No more yelling in my ear. No more nips for attention. She made herself at home and continued observing me as I got to work this morning.

I’ve grown up with cats all my life. I’m 35, and I feel so silly for not even considering this prior to now. I’m always learning something new with these guys!

Edit - I’m loving all your stories and pictures of your own desk setups for the cats! It’s so fun to see how everyone has accommodated their own little supurrvisors. Thank you for sharing and teaching me a new way to keep my cats happy!

text:
Am I being unreasonable for wanting to bail on an overnight backpacking trip because I’m worried about my cat? I’m supposed to go backpacking tomorrow with a friend and a few other people. We’d be gone for around 36 hours, and there would be no cell service, so I wouldn’t be able to check on my cat while I’m gone.

My cat is 11, and she’s currently staying with me at a friend’s place while I’m traveling. She’s been doing fine here, eating and drinking normally and mostly back to her usual self after the drive. I don’t have any reason to think something is wrong, but I’m still really anxious about leaving her alone for that long. I might be able to get someone to check on her, but I’m not sure how comfortable I feel relying on that, and I wouldn’t be able to check in myself because of the lack of service.

Part of me thinks I’m being ridiculous because she’s been fine here and it’s only one night, but another part of me feels genuinely uncomfortable leaving her without being able to check on her. I also feel awkward backing out at the last minute when my friend and several other people are going. I thought backpacking would be fun, and I feel like I should go, but now I’m questioning whether I’ll even enjoy myself because I’ll be worrying about her the whole time.

Would you go, or would you bail and just do a day hike instead? Am I overthinking this, or is it reasonable to decide I’m not comfortable leaving her alone that long?

text: Do cats have their own little schedule? I was laying in bed a few minutes ago and saw one of my cats suddenly leap off the bed and race into the hall. It got me thinking: was he late for an appointment or did he forget something from earlier in his day that he suddenly recalled? 🤣 I know cats don’t view time in the same way humans do since they obviously can’t tell time with a clock, but are they able to make their own schedules? Like when I’m at work during the day do they plan out how they’re going to spend their day napping, window watching, scratching the coffee table, 💩 time, etc? or do they just live in the moment and act as the mood strikes them? I love watching them lounge and then suddenly jump off the bed and prance into the living room, only to stand there like they forgot what they were doing. Worried about elderly cat getting out when company comes over Ok so my cat is 18 years old. Her name is Sunny. I absolutely cherish her and she adores me. I wish I could upload photos because our bond is truly something else.

My dad has family coming over next week for 3.5 days. It’s a Mormon family, so 2 adults and I believe 6-7 children between 2-10 years old. She is obviously going to feel stressed and overstimulated. My biggest concern though, is anyone- including my dad who is hosting this thing- leaving the front door open due to being distracted, and Sunny either bolting outside (she has obvious cognitive decline, developing cataracts, and can’t hear very well at all. I have to be careful greeting her because she gets easily startled because she can’t hear me approaching) where she could get lost and NOT FIND HER WAY BACK HOME, or people being oblivious, or kids being kids, and shutting her outside by mistake or ignorance and forgetfulness or mindlessness of the boundaries I am going to set as far as leaving the front door open. If she gets out and strays from the house, she WILL NOT BE ABLE TO FIND HER WAY BACK HOME. it’s every animal owners worst fear, right? Never knowing or having any idea how this thing you deeply love is doing. If it’s ok. Where it is.

So basically, big risk with so many kids coming over.
My dad is in his 60s, but has the emotional intelligence of a carrot, or any other vegetable really. He is basically like a young teenager when it comes to confrontation and he does not take many of the safeguards seriously when it comes to Sunny. Despite me showing studies and evidence about the risks and limitations of a super elderly cat, he doesn’t agree, and you can tell he doesn’t buy some things I say AT ALL. how he felt about something beforehand is all the evidence he needs to feel completely justified and valid about things. He is right because he feels he is right. I don’t trust him to be careful with the front door or the kids not overwhelming her at all. He thinks I am being WAY TOO overprotective, despite me referencing and trying to show the studies. Acute stress can absolutely cause physical damage to an 18 year old cat ( such as a bunch of kids pestering her for 3 days). He doesn’t buy that. I showed him evidence and he just rolls his eyes and he says “ok” sarcastically. In his mind I’m being overboard protective. Evidence doesn’t matter. He doesn’t believe the cat could be a flight risk with stress being inside and the door being left open. I don’t think he’s been receptive to anything anyone has ever said except his mom or religious figures.

WHAT CAN I DO TO SAFEGUARD THE CAT while I am at work??! I am thinking of buying one of those dog gates they use to keep dogs out of certain rooms. There is the front door, a small porch, and then an entry to the small stairs leading off the porch. I can put the gate there at the top of the stairs. She is too old to easily jump on top of the porch fence and over very easily or quickly. It’s at least a buffer. I am also thinking about moving the litter box from the garage to my room as well so she doesn’t have to walk through the madness of 6-7 small children to do her business.

Is there anything else I can do to safeguard Sunny for the 9-13 hours I am at work for those few days?! I’m genuinely scared and spiraling about this. Sitting down and trying to have a rational conversation about my concerns with my dad (who will be the only one home all day for this as he is retired) will be about as productive as trying to set boundaries with an angry 13 year old teenager. I’m not exaggerating the dude needs therapy.

TL/DR: my kitty is 18 years old and cannot navigate or survive outside anymore. A bunch of family the cat has never met, between the ages of 2-10, are coming over for a few days during my work week. I can’t trust my dad to be as careful as believe I need him to be to ensure the front door isn’t left open by anyone and the kids don’t overstimulate her. What can I do to safeguard the kitty’s safety while me and my mom are both at work?
label: accomodation

The times she has been responsive her responses seem like the pick up date is being pushed back more and more. It’s now Oct 26 and she’s just ghost mode.

I live in Illinois and can’t find any laws about pet abandonment in relation to a situation like this. When would the cat be considered abandoned and could be legally owned by me. My partner and I have grown attached to the cat and her owner’s behavior is showing us that she isn’t actually invested in her cat. She’s only interesting in reaching out to see her cat when it’s extremely convenient for her.
